title: The switch test
scenario: The studio checks how hard it would be to move its linked set-up to another AI vendor next year. You decide what is easy to move and what is not. Use the exhibit. The sheet is made up for this case. The rule lines come from the docs.
exhibit:
CONNECTION SHEET (made up for this case):
  Design    A design vendor's remote MCP server. The vendor's install page
            gives steps for Claude Code, Codex by OpenAI, Cursor and VS Code.
  Masters   The approved master files. Kept only in one AI vendor's file store.
  Library   A standard remote MCP server run by the library vendor.
  Posting   A scheduler flow that relies on pinning the tool list. Pinning is
            a Claude API beta.
  Demo      A vendor demo of an interactive MCP App panel inside a chat. It was
            tested in one AI app only.

NEXT YEAR (made up for this case):
  The client may ask the studio to move the whole set-up to another AI vendor.

VENDOR LINES (copied from the docs):
  MCP specification: "Extensions are always opt-in and require explicit support
  from both client and server, negotiated during initialization."

questions.prompt: Which connection will be the easiest to move to another AI vendor?

options.text: Masters, because a vendor's file store can be copied to any other vendor in one step
options.explanation: Files in one vendor's store are not part of an open standard. Moving them takes work.

options.text: Design, because a standard remote server can be used from AI apps of several vendors
options.explanation: Right. The MCP site says to build once and integrate everywhere, and the vendor's page lists clients from several vendors.

options.text: Posting, because a pinned tool list is a standard part of every vendor's MCP set-up
options.explanation: The cited pages describe a pin for Anthropic's beta only. It is not in the others.

options.text: Demo, because an interactive panel looks the same in every AI app that the client uses
options.explanation: Extensions need support from both client and server. The panel was tested in one app only.

questions.prompt: The masters live only in one vendor's file store. What is the better plan?

options.text: Keep the masters in the studio's own storage, and treat any vendor store as a copy
options.explanation: Right. This is our exit plan: master files and records stay in storage the studio controls.

options.text: Keep the vendor's store as the master copy, because it is the safest place for the studio
options.explanation: A vendor's file store is a copy. If the vendor changes terms or ends a feature, the studio is stuck.

options.text: Keep the masters in two different vendors' stores, so that each one backs up the other
options.explanation: Two vendors' stores are still two copies at vendors. The studio does not hold a master.

options.text: Keep the masters nowhere, and ask the AI to make them again from scratch when needed
options.explanation: Remaking an approved master loses the approved file. A copy in studio storage is simple.

questions.prompt: The posting flow relies on the tool-list pin. The client asks for the same flow on Gemini. What do you say?

options.text: It will work the same way, because pinning is part of the MCP standard that Gemini follows
options.explanation: The pin is described on Anthropic's beta page. The cited Gemini page does not describe one.

options.text: It cannot work at all, because Gemini does not support MCP in any form or on any page
options.explanation: Gemini's docs describe Remote MCP with Streamable HTTP. It can be used.

options.text: Check what Gemini offers, and keep a record of the approved tool list in case it has no pin
options.explanation: Right. The cited Gemini page describes allowed_tools but no pin. Treat the pin as a Claude-only extra and keep your own record.

options.text: Switch the whole studio to Claude, since that is the only vendor with a beta feature
options.explanation: One beta feature is a thin reason. It also deepens the lock-in.

questions.prompt: A client loves the interactive MCP App panel from the demo. Will it work in every AI app?

options.text: Yes, because MCP is a standard, so every client shows every extension in the same way
options.explanation: Extensions are opt-in. Both client and server must support them.

options.text: Yes, if the server's owner is a big company, since big servers are tested everywhere
options.explanation: Size does not decide it. Support must be negotiated by client and server.

options.text: No, because an interactive panel can only be shown inside a web browser tab
options.explanation: The spec does not say that. The limit is support on both sides.

options.text: Not sure, because extensions are opt-in, so ask which AI apps the demo was tested in
options.explanation: Right. The spec says extensions need explicit support from both client and server, negotiated at the start.
